testCases.input: what is vibe testing and why isn't it enough for deploying an llm app?
testCases.actualOutput:
To understand vibe testing, the intuitive idea behind it is simply trying out an application casually, just like testing the "vibe" of something by asking a handful of questions and relying on your personal feeling to decide if the answers are right. Technically speaking, vibe testing is an informal, subjective, and usually non-repeatable evaluation method where you test a Large Language Model (LLM) application with just a few prompts—typically around four to ten questions that happen to come to your mind—and assume the application works properly if those few responses look good. 

This approach is not enough for deploying a production-grade LLM application in the industry for a couple of key reasons. First, because it relies entirely on your personal, subjective judgment at a single moment in time, it is not repeatable; if you return to test the application ten days later, you will likely ask completely different questions rather than the exact same ones. Second, because it only involves a tiny handful of ad-hoc queries, it fails to provide the rigorous, methodological evaluation required to ensure a software application is truly robust, safe, and ready for real-world deployment beyond a personal project level.
